cohort: 192 obstetric patients who received general anesthesia for cesarean delivery between January 2010 and December 2014
finding: The second-generation laryngeal mask airway (LMA) was found to be a viable option for obstetric anesthesia, with no significant differences in neonatal Apgar scores or maternal and neonatal postoperative outcomes compared to endotracheal intubation.
mod_finding: This study evaluated the use of laryngeal mask airways (LMA) versus endotracheal intubation (ET) for cesarean deliveries requiring general anesthesia, finding that LMA is a viable option in certain cases.
